title: Discovery of two novel small-molecule series with potent SARS-CoV-2 inhibition via putative nsp13 open-state trapping
summary: A trained message-passing neural network prioritized compounds for experimental testing, leading to a reported new scaffold and two antiviral series. Cell-based assays found antiviral activity among tested compounds; the paper states that direct target engagement is unvalidated, so the proposed mechanism remains provisional.
ai_technology: A trained message-passing neural network prioritizes candidate compounds for experimental evaluation.
organization: University of California San Diego; Herbert Wertheim UF Scripps Institute; University of Louisville

evidence.tested: The computational-to-experimental screen reports 31 compounds meeting its cell-based antiviral-potency criterion among 60 with complete measurements.
evidence.unknown: Cell-based activity is reported, but direct engagement of the proposed viral target is not experimentally established; no operational compound details are included here.
evidence.ai_role: The learned model prioritized candidates that led to measured cell-based antiviral activity.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
